newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Mubarak regret Mideast peace freeze.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Mubarak regret Mideast peace freeze.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac held talks with his Egyptian counterpart Hosni Mubarak on Middle East peace on Thursday and said they regretted a freeze in the peace process.

"I am happy to note once again that we agree on everything, particularly on the peace process...and we regret there is an unfortunate freeze in the current situation," Chirac told reporters after the talks in Paris.
The French leader warned of "the danger that all this represents for the stability of the region", adding that peace was "possible, necessary and urgent".
Chirac said he would bring up Arab-Israeli peace in meetings with U.S. President Bill Clinton as well as at a summit of the world's most industrialised countries in Denver on Friday.
Mubarak, who stayed in Paris just two hours, said he hoped "Israelis and Palestinians would find a position that would allow peace talks to resume."
Chirac aides said the two "noted a certain American disengagement (from the peace process), an unchanged attitude by Israeli authorities and therefore a considerable risk to peace."
Mubarak's visit came after European Union leaders backed his mediation efforts to revive Israeli-Palestinian peace talks and pledged to support his initiative.

In a "European Call for Peace in the Middle East" adopted at their Amsterdam summit earlier this week, they warned that stagnation on the Palestinian, Syrian and Lebanese negotiating tracks "is a permanent threat to the security of all" and urged the peoples and governments of the Middle East to renew talks.
They urged Israel for the first time to consider allowing the creation of a Palestinian state and reaffirmed opposition to Israeli settlements beyond that country's pre-June 1967 borders.
They also called on the Palestinian people to reaffirm their commitment to the legitimate right of Israel to live within safe and recognised borders.
